scope: MoE systems methods/evaluation; fixed-residency exact-routing inference relevance, including training ancestry and explicitly separated offloading/transport/architecture changes.
counting_rule: Only verified conference publication with retrieved methods and evaluation full text is included. Supplementary preprints and access-limited conference papers do not count.

papers.title: DeepSpeed-MoE: Advancing Mixture-of-Experts Inference and Training to Power Next-Generation AI Scale
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Multidimensional parallelism and specialized kernels can exploit aggregate memory bandwidth for low-latency MoE inference; architecture compression is a separate hypothesis.
papers.mechanism: Expert/tensor/data parallelism, expert slicing, hierarchical all-to-all, coordinated communication and sparse gating kernels. PR-MoE and mixture-of-students also change architecture/model size and must be separated from the execution-only path.
papers.model_hardware: 52B standard MoE (1.3B base, 128 experts), larger 1T/2T inference configurations; NVIDIA A100 Azure clusters. Standard 52B scaling uses 8–64 GPUs; larger comparisons reach hundreds.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: Training/quality experiments include pretrained language-model data and zero-shot tasks. Inference scaling uses configured model/batch shapes; natural request-arrival trace construction is not reported in §5.2.
papers.baselines: PyTorch MoE; dense models and PR-MoE/MoS variants in separate quality/cost comparisons.
papers.controls: Standard-MoE execution comparison holds model fixed; architecture/distillation gains are separately plotted. GPU counts differ in some cost-equivalent dense comparisons.
papers.experimental_unit: Configured model/parallelism/GPU-count benchmark, not an independently sampled serving session.
papers.metrics_timing: Inference latency and tokens/s; system/kernel optimizations. Open-loop queueing, request-tail latency and timing-repetition protocol not specified in read §5.2.
papers.reported_results: §5.2/Fig.7 reports up to 7.3× latency/throughput improvement for trillion-parameter models; this combines multiple system changes and is not a replica-dispatch-only gain.
papers.ablations: Scaling and standard versus PR-MoE/MoS comparisons; Appendix C configurations.
papers.limits: Different model scale, network and communication collectives; exact serving arrival process absent. Quality-equivalent dense comparisons do not imply identical arithmetic.
papers.artifact_availability: Public project named by paper; historical paper configuration not independently executed or fully audited in this review.
papers.relevance: Foundational execution/communication baseline. Replicated input plus output allreduce omits the token all-to-all being optimized here.

papers.title: Tutel: Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts at Scale
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Preserving parameter layout across parallel/pipeline modes permits low-overhead runtime adaptation to MoE workload variation.
papers.mechanism: Identical tensor layout across expert/data parallel modes, dynamic pipelining, fast encode/decode and hierarchical all-to-all.
papers.model_hardware: Up to 2,048 A100 SXM 80GB GPUs (8 per Azure VM, 1,600-Gbps aggregate interconnect); single-layer grids and SwinV2-MoE.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: 243 single-layer configurations and capacity-factor variation as a workload proxy; ImageNet and COCO for vision-model training/inference quality. These are not natural request-arrival traces.
papers.baselines: Fairseq MoE and static parallel/pipeline alternatives; framework versions and parallelism are specified.
papers.controls: Matched parallelism for direct comparisons, then incremental optimizations; capacity and pipeline modes varied explicitly.
papers.experimental_unit: Layer configuration or model/device-count experiment; repeated iterations within a configuration.
papers.metrics_timing: Layer step latency/throughput, end-to-end model training and inference throughput, memory and accuracy.
papers.reported_results: Paper reports 4.96× speedup at 16 GPUs and 5.75× at 2,048 GPUs for layer benchmarks; SwinV2-MoE training/inference improvements are 1.55×/2.11×. Different denominators must not be pooled.
papers.ablations: Feature-addition Fig.14; adaptive versus static modes; Appendix B kernels and Appendix C capacity/top-k/expert variations.
papers.limits: Scale and training/vision workloads differ; capacity-factor stress does not reproduce measured LLM temporal routing. Current repository has evolved since paper.
papers.artifact_availability: README and source tree inspected at f6610fd55b6b694ad9f033306b87cf37468f87c3; public implementation, no reproduction run.
papers.relevance: Useful for separating matched execution controls from adaptivity claims and for exposing communication costs absent from the present allreduce harness.
papers.fulltext_version: Author arXiv full text corresponding to verified MLSys publication

papers.title: MegaBlocks: Efficient Sparse Training with Mixture-of-Experts
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Block-sparse execution can retain every routed token without the large padding cost of batched GEMM.
papers.mechanism: Reformulates MoE as block-sparse matrix products with custom sparse formats and kernels; rounds per-expert token count to a block of 128 rather than padding every expert to a common maximum.
papers.model_hardware: GPT-style XS–Medium models, 64 experts and top-1 routing; 8 A100 SXM4 80GB GPUs, CUDA11.5/CUTLASS2.5.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: The Pile training and validation; layer microbenchmarks with training-sized expert token groups. Paper expects thousands of tokens/expert, unlike B128 inference.
papers.baselines: Tutel integrated into the same Megatron framework and dense Megatron models.
papers.controls: Dropless and token-dropping Tutel comparisons distinguished; common global batch512 while memory capacity permits different microbatch sizes; validation loss accompanies speed.
papers.experimental_unit: Model/configuration training run or layer microbenchmark, not arrival-seed block.
papers.metrics_timing: Full training wall time and validation loss; §6.3 microbenchmark averages100 kernel executions but EXCLUDES sparse-metadata construction, arguing amortization across six operations. Do not use that microbenchmark as all-overhead latency.
papers.reported_results: Up to 40% over the best Tutel configurations and 1.8–2.4× relative to dense models at comparable validation loss. Dropless-only comparisons have larger gains and are a different claim.
papers.ablations: §6.1 dropless versus capacity-padded training; §6.2 loss-equivalent token-dropping comparisons; §6.3 uniform-routing kernel benchmark and tile-order/cache sensitivity. The retrieved manuscript has no appendices.
papers.limits: Training and large token groups; padding-count reductions alone do not establish latency. Architecture/model-quality comparisons differ from exact-layer route preservation.
papers.artifact_availability: Current README and source tree inspected at952db33d6eac334d22c61e47a0d5d41446298784; dmoe.py and BF16 forward tests subsequently inspected. Public code, no reproduction run; no archival DOI asserted.
papers.relevance: Strong precedent for measuring grouped expert execution, but its 128-token blocks and training groups do not establish a benefit for the current small BF16 experts.
papers.fulltext_version: Author arXiv full text corresponding to MLSys proceedings

papers.title: SmartMoE: Efficiently Training Sparsely-Activated Models through Combining Offline and Online Parallelization
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: An offline pool of good hybrid parallel configurations plus online expert remapping can adapt to changing expert popularity at lower search cost.
papers.mechanism: Cost-model-guided hybrid DP/TP/PP/EP search and online remapping. §6.2 uses a predicted-load improvement threshold, prefers mappings near the current placement in ties, and tunes search frequency empirically.
papers.model_hardware: 32 V100 PCIe/50-Gbps, 64 V100 SXM/100-Gbps and 32 A100 SXM/200-Gbps clusters; GPT-MoE 4.5–14B and Swin-MoE.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: Actual model-training routing traces and capacity factors1.2/2.4/4.8/infinite. Exact source dataset names for all system sweeps were not established in this extraction.
papers.baselines: DeepSpeed-MoE, Tutel, manually tuned FasterMoE, and an Alpa strategy reimplementation in PyTorch (not the JAX system itself).
papers.controls: Training iteration includes forward/backward/gradient synchronization/optimizer and dense layers; separate offline/online controls; weak scaling changes total model size.
papers.experimental_unit: Model/hardware/configuration training experiment; source-token traces, not open-loop serving sessions.
papers.metrics_timing: Full training iteration time and throughput, memory, model search overhead and cost prediction.
papers.reported_results: Up to 1.88× over FasterMoE; reported average speedups depend on cluster/model (e.g.1.53× A100 and1.17× V100-SXM GPT workloads).
papers.ablations: Offline versus online components, cost-model accuracy and search interval; §7.4 reports the trade-off between adjustment cost and stale mappings.
papers.limits: Training, mutable placement and different parallelism. Thresholded rebalancing and stability/cost concerns already exist; a new threshold alone has little novelty.
papers.artifact_availability: README/source tree inspected at e19b3a994db5f7614778fd02c48f602ba9d9ac6e; available artifact, not executed.
papers.relevance: Direct prior art for proposed reconfiguration gates; also motivates charging planner/commit overhead and identifying whether mappings actually change.

papers.title: Accelerating Distributed MoE Training and Inference with Lina
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Coordinating communication priorities and using expert popularity/prediction can mitigate contention and imbalance in distributed MoE.
papers.mechanism: Training communication scheduling; inference expert-selection path estimation, hot-expert replication/cold packing and pipelined CPU–GPU expert loading. Prediction mismatch requires a correction before dependent compute.
papers.model_hardware: 4 nodes×4 A10040GB, 100-Gbps InfiniBand; Transformer-XL, GPT2 and BERT-related MoE models, 2–16 experts; inference top-1 versus training top-2.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: Enwik8 text generation and WMT English–German for inference; additional training/model tasks in §7.1/Table6.
papers.baselines: Vanilla DeepSpeed and a separate Tutel comparison. §7.1 explicitly enables hierarchical all-to-all for Lina and DeepSpeed; it does not state this for Tutel. An ideal balanced-gate reference changes logical routing and is identified as an idealization.
papers.controls: Token dropping disabled; 10 warmup/50 measured training iterations. Five inference executions split into two unprofiled timings and three profiler runs to prevent profiler perturbation of the latency result.
papers.experimental_unit: Model/test-set batch benchmark; individual test-set batches are not independently randomized systems.
papers.metrics_timing: End-to-end batch median/p95 inference latency; training iteration time and profiler breakdown in separate runs.
papers.reported_results: §7.3 reports median improvements of1.54× and1.45× for Transformer-XL with4/16experts;16expert p95 improvements1.82× (TXL) and1.68× (BERT).
papers.ablations: No prediction, no fine tuning, expert-path length1/3/6 and tasks; training communication components.
papers.limits: Inference includes offloading/prefetch and model-specific path prediction, unlike permanently resident experts. Ideal-gate references are not exact-routing controls.
papers.artifact_availability: No dedicated downloadable Lina implementation verified in this review; cited upstream DeepSpeed/Tutel are not substitutes for its artifact.
papers.relevance: Transfers the discipline of separating profiled diagnosis from unprofiled completion time; exact-route replicated-input comparisons cannot claim its distributed-serving scope.

papers.title: Fiddler: CPU-GPU Orchestration for Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Models
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: For sparse decode, computing cold experts on the CPU can be cheaper than repeatedly transferring full expert weights to the GPU.
papers.mechanism: Offline hot-expert placement and CPU/GPU execution selection from measured cost; custom CPU BF16 computation and transfer overlap.
papers.model_hardware: Uncompressed16-bit Mixtral8×7B;24GB Quadro RTX6000+Xeon6126 and49GB RTX6000Ada+Xeon8480+; appendix Phi3.5-MoE.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: ShareGPT conversations for calibration/evaluation; Appendix D repeats with LMSYS. Input/output length sweeps and beam-search widths are constructed workloads.
papers.baselines: DeepSpeed-MIIv0.2.3/ZeRO offload, Mixtral-Offloading modified to unquantized16-bit, tuned llama.cpp b2956.
papers.controls: Same weight precision; best disclosed baseline offload configuration; hardware platforms separated. CPU instruction support and GPU-resident expert fractions differ by platform.
papers.experimental_unit: Prompt/configuration single-request generation experiment; not production request stream.
papers.metrics_timing: Prefill and decoding tokens/s, TTFT and inter-token latency; input32–4096/output64–512 and beam4/8/12/16.
papers.reported_results: Reported average1.26× over the best baseline in decoding; much larger beam-search comparisons use different regimes. Appendix F separately reports TTFT1.13× and ITL1.43×.
papers.ablations: CPU/GPU offload choices, long prefill, beam widths, second dataset and second model.
papers.limits: Capacity-constrained offloading, not all-resident two-H100 execution. Single-request throughput cannot establish queueing-tail generalization.
papers.artifact_availability: README/source tree inspected at 227715bfd6e8c731b29548eab01d9919c4fe9564; public implementation, no execution.
papers.relevance: Supports measuring transfer versus compute costs and calibrating on independent prompts; its CPU execution mechanism does not apply directly to current resident replicas.
papers.fulltext_version: Author arXiv version with ICLR2025 header and appendices

papers.title: MoE-Lightning: High-Throughput MoE Inference on Memory-constrained GPUs
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Offloading choices should follow the CPU/GPU/interconnect bottleneck jointly rather than minimizing weight transfers alone.
papers.mechanism: Hierarchical roofline model and CGOPipe paged-weight CPU/GPU/I/O pipeline; policy selects microbatching, attention placement and GPU weight residency.
papers.model_hardware: Mixtral8×7B on single T4/L4;8×22B and DBRX on2–4 T4;24/32CPUcores and192/416GB host memory.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: MT-Bench80prompts replicated for offline batching; HELM synthetic-reasoning/summarization workloads; output lengths32/64/128/256.
papers.baselines: FlexGen with CPU-attention option and DeepSpeed ZeRO-Inference0.14.3.
papers.controls: A padded MoE-Lightning variant matches FlexGen padding; maximal feasible batch sizes differ between systems, explicitly part of the throughput objective.
papers.experimental_unit: Offline batch/model/hardware configuration, not arrival-seed trial.
papers.metrics_timing: Tokens divided by full prefill+decode elapsed time, memory and policy efficiency. No open-loop queueing claim.
papers.reported_results: Up to10.3× against the best baseline in the broad throughput setup; padding-matched comparison is smaller (up to3.5× versus FlexGen).
papers.ablations: CPU attention/FFN/KV choices, policy selection and hardware bottleneck regimes.
papers.limits: Host-offloading and batch-capacity gains do not transfer to fixed-budget fully resident experts; replicated prompts are not independent workload samples.
papers.artifact_availability: No repository was independently inspected for this paper in the present review; do not infer reproducibility from the manuscript alone.
papers.relevance: Strong model for declaring the bottleneck and reporting matched-capacity controls, but a different optimization problem from resident-copy dispatch.
papers.fulltext_version: Author arXiv manuscript; conference identity/DOI verified separately

papers.experimental_unit: Model/task/configuration; no independently sampled serving-arrival units.
papers.metrics_timing: MoE-block latency, end-to-end inference throughput, peak memory and task quality.

papers.relevance: Illustrates need to separate algorithmic changes requiring quality evaluation from physical-copy reassignment that preserves experts and combining weights.
papers.fulltext_version: Author arXiv full text with artifact appendix; ISCA DOI verified

papers.title: FlashMoE: Fast Distributed MoE in a Single Kernel
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Device-side persistent scheduling can avoid CPU launch bottlenecks and overlap distributed MoE data movement at finer granularity.
papers.mechanism: Single persistent GPU kernel combines dispatch, expert computation and combine with NVSHMEM communication and locality-aware dependency scheduling.
papers.model_hardware: 8 H10080GB over NVLink; main layer shapes hidden/intermediate2048,top2,up to128experts and16Ktokens; additional A100/V100 diagnostics.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: MoE-layer shape/configuration workloads; not a complete serving request trace. Appendix workload construction must not be treated as full Qwen serving.
papers.controls: 32 warmups then average32timed executions. Paper uses FP32 for FlashMoE and FP16 for other systems, an explicit precision mismatch. COMET8GPU case excluded by authors for anomalously poor performance.
papers.experimental_unit: Single-layer configuration/microbenchmark; repeated kernel calls are technical repeats.
papers.metrics_timing: MoE forward latency, throughput, SM activity, overlap and scaling. SM activity and concurrent GPU durations are not exclusive fractions of wall time.
papers.reported_results: Reported maxima:6× latency improvement,5.7× throughput and9× SM-activity improvement. They are layer/microbenchmark results under the stated controls, not general serving response gains.
papers.ablations: Appendix A timing/setup; appendices G/H implementation/limitations; hardware/scale and straggler diagnostics.
papers.limits: Transport, scheduling and compute change together; precision mismatch limits causal isolation. Persistent NVSHMEM path is not a drop-in replacement for output-allreduce harness.
papers.artifact_availability: README and source tree inspected at9cc0c32443d2a2da6825a68af5ef83060329483b; public CUDA/NVSHMEM code, not executed.
papers.relevance: Closest conference evidence for host-scheduling overhead, but a direct comparison must align precision, token groups and communication path.
papers.fulltext_version: arXivv3; verified NeurIPS proceedings identity. Erroneous initial ID2506.04556 was rejected and excluded.

papers.title: Occult: Optimizing Collaborative Communications across Experts for Accelerated Parallel MoE Training and Inference
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Expert coactivation structure can reduce redundant inter-device communication, with optional routing pruning providing further gains.
papers.mechanism: Collaborative token communication and coactivation-aware expert placement; separate collaboration-pruning mode restricts selected devices and fine-tunes routing.

papers.relevance: Useful matched-logical-routing boundary: only the unpruned physical path is eligible for an exact arithmetic comparison with the current dispatcher.

papers.title: LocMoE: A Low-Overhead MoE for Large Language Model Training

papers.title: Janus: A Unified Distributed Training Framework for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Models
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.

papers.datasets_trace_construction: Configured training models and batch/sequence sweeps; source dataset names not established in read system-evaluation paragraphs.

papers.title: SonicMoE: Accelerating MoE with IO and Tile-aware Optimizations

papers.title: MegaScale-Infer: Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Model Serving with Disaggregated Expert Parallelism

papers.mechanism: Different parallelism/hardware for attention and FFNs; ping-pong microbatches; CPU-proxy/GDRCopy RDMA; §6 floor-cost expert model C_j=sum_i x_ij max(a_i,K) and greedy replica placement from traffic.
papers.model_hardware: Homogeneous8nodes×8Ampere80GB,400GB/sNVLink and8×200GbpsNICs; heterogeneousH20/L40S. BF16Mixtral8×22B,DBRX and317B scaled MoE.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: Private production request trace with median input571/output159; configured microbatch and shape sweeps.
papers.baselines: vLLM and TensorRT-LLM; component and deployment variants.
papers.controls: Decode and prefill measured separately across systems, with end-to-end throughput also reported; throughput optimized under TBT150ms constraint. Disaggregation can increase individual microbatch latency.
papers.experimental_unit: Model/deployment/workload configuration; private trace replay, not independent public source blocks.
papers.metrics_timing: Per-GPU/cost throughput, time between tokens, prefill/decode latency and M2N median/tail latency.
papers.reported_results: Up to1.90× per-GPU serving throughput versus TensorRT-LLM within the paper’s latency constraints; multi-component system result.
papers.ablations: Disaggregation, M2N transport, pipeline and heterogeneous deployment; workload/scale sensitivities.
papers.limits: Private workload and substantial transport/architecture changes. Floor cost already recognizes activated-expert overhead; the current generic insight is not novel.
papers.artifact_availability: Paper references constituent public communication libraries, but a complete system plus private request trace was not verified as available.
papers.relevance: Closest conference precedent for nonlinear expert cost and serving-level controls; present allreduce layer omits its attention, transport and scheduling costs.
papers.fulltext_version: Author manuscript titled Serving Mixture-of-Experts at Scale with Disaggregated Expert Parallelism; conference title and DOI separately verified

papers.title: GShard: Scaling Giant Models with Conditional Computation and Automatic Sharding
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Conditional expert computation plus automatic SPMD sharding can scale model capacity more cheaply than dense computation.
papers.mechanism: Groupwise top-2 routing with capacity constraints, auxiliary load balance and probabilistic second expert; XLA/SPMD tensor-sharding annotations and distributed expert execution.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: In-house25B parallel examples across100languages,13B intoEnglish;1Ttraining tokens. Proprietary multilingual quality/test sets.
papers.baselines: Bilingual models and dense96-layer GPipe; model/depth/expert scaling variants.
papers.controls: BLEU and training cost evaluated together; scaling changes model capacity. Main successful large runs useFP32; BF16trillion-model instability is disclosed.
papers.experimental_unit: Training model/scale/language configuration, not serving arrival unit.
papers.metrics_timing: Training step time, memory/scaling, BLEU and total training cost.
papers.reported_results: 600B model trained in4days on2048TPUv3 cores; scaling16×parameters costs roughly3.6× in the cited comparisons.
papers.ablations: Depth and expert-count trade-offs, memory/communication scaling and multilingual quality.
papers.limits: Training, private corpus and TPU architecture; logical routing changes and token capacity differ from exact fixed checkpoint inference.
papers.artifact_availability: No complete model/data/system reproduction artifact verified here; compiler concepts and author publication are public.
papers.relevance: Foundational definition of logical routing/capacity and why dropping/altering tokens must not be hidden within a systems speedup.
papers.fulltext_version: Author manuscript with accepted ICLR identity verified from OpenReview/Google Research

papers.title: Lancet: Accelerating Mixture-of-Experts Training via Whole Graph Computation-Communication Overlapping
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Whole-graph dependency-aware scheduling can overlap communication beyond the expert layer while preserving routing semantics.
papers.mechanism: Compiler schedules weight gradients and dynamically selects operator partitions using cached operation/communication profiles. Capacity information passes between partitions to preserve exact token-to-expert mapping and dropping; irregular all-to-all sends only actual tokens.
papers.model_hardware: 8nodes each of A10080GB p4de or V100 p3dn;64GPUs maximum; GPT2-S/L MoE with2experts/GPU.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: WikiText input, sequence512; largest stated fitting batch per model/hardware; Switch and batch-prioritized gates.
papers.baselines: DeepSpeed0.5.8,Tutel0.3 with best overlap degree1/2/4/8, and common RAF compiler without Lancet to control framework differences.
papers.controls: Same RAF baseline isolates compilation/scheduling; both gate types constrain legal partitioning; weak scaling keeps local batch fixed.
papers.experimental_unit: Model/gate/GPU-count training configuration; timing repetition/independent-run uncertainty not reported in read §7.
papers.metrics_timing: Full training iteration time/throughput, overlapped/non-overlapped operation durations, cost prediction and optimization time.
papers.reported_results: Up to1.30× with Switch gating on V100; mean1.17×A100 and1.22×V100 for that setting. Computation time can increase due to partition overhead while wall time decreases.
papers.ablations: Gate types and hardware; cost prediction error3.83%; optimizer time; overlap/dependency analysis.
papers.limits: Training backward work supplies overlap absent in layer inference; summed overlap components must not be treated as additive wall-time shares.
papers.artifact_availability: Uses open RAF/TVM but a dedicated Lancet repository was not verified in this bounded review.
papers.relevance: Strong exact-routing precedent and common-framework control; timing benefit can coexist with more total work, so active/padded counts are mechanism proxies, not latency proof.
papers.fulltext_version: Author manuscript corresponding to MLSys2024 publication

papers.title: COMET: Fine-grained Computation-communication Overlapping for Mixture-of-Experts
papers.uncertainty: No independent-run confidence interval or experimental-unit resampling identified in the cited evaluation sections; iteration averages are not independent workload samples.
papers.hypothesis: Tile-granular dependency resolution and calibrated resource allocation can hide communication and host scheduling overhead without sacrificing grouped-GEMM efficiency.
papers.mechanism: Splits shared tensors along independent dimensions, schedules local-ready tiles first, horizontally fuses communication/compute, and profiles a fixed configuration-specific resource split before deployment.
papers.datasets_trace_construction: Input token-length/model/parallelism sweeps; synthetic imbalance varied by token-distribution standard deviation with a production-training reference std0.032. Natural serving arrival trace not provided.
papers.baselines: Common Megatron-LM6dbe4c with CUTLASS,TransformerEngine,Tutel andFasterMoE; FasterMoE limited to expert parallelism.
papers.controls: Attention implementation identical across end-to-end comparisons; separate single-layer and whole-model results; NVSHMEM memory overhead reported.
papers.experimental_unit: Layer/model/shape/parallelism benchmark; independent-run CI and repetition count not identified in read §5.
papers.metrics_timing: MoE/full-model latency, communication overlap, host overhead and memory; local indexing/dispatch counted as computation rather than GPU–GPU communication.
papers.reported_results: §5.2 average full-model latency reductions31.8% versusTutel and34.1% versusMegatron-CUTLASS; layer speedups1.28–2.37×. They include changed communication and scheduling.
papers.ablations: Token length, expert/top-k, parallelism, imbalance, NVLink versusPCIe and memory overhead; offline resource-split profiling.
papers.limits: Most groups are much larger than current small-layer inference; communication fusion changes the intervention. Production trace is only a distribution reference.
papers.artifact_availability: Paper-linked public Flux repository; README retrieval/commit recorded separately. Whole artifact not executed. Actual repository README inspected at 19831ca2d820e3e782ed1d15d8b52d0898b78b26.
papers.relevance: Most useful matched-framework control and direct warning that host dispatch overhead can dominate small expert groups; current output-allreduce does not test its full communication mechanism.
papers.fulltext_version: Author manuscript corresponding to MLSys2025 proceedings
